text.headline: Brushy Canyon research
text.text: A TimelineJS view of events tagged Brushy Canyon Formation in The West Face dataset — names, maps, process models, and Mines theses.

background.alt: King 1948 USGS Professional Paper 215 plate — El Capitan to Shumard Peak

text.headline: King — Brushy Cherry and Bell Canyon named
text.text:
P. B. King describes the Delaware Mountain Group and its Brushy Canyon, Cherry Canyon, and Bell Canyon Formations (names already credited to him in DeFord and Lloyd, 1940). Formal lithostratigraphic frame for the western escarpment and Delaware Basin fill.

People: Philip B. King

King, P.B., 1942, Permian of west Texas and southeastern New Mexico: AAPG Bulletin, v. 26, no. 4, p. 535–763. See also DeFord, R.K., and Lloyd, E.R., 1940, AAPG Bulletin, v. 24, p. 1–14 (names credited to King).

text.headline: King — USGS Professional Paper 215 southern Guadalupes
text.text:
USGS Professional Paper 215 maps and describes the southern Guadalupe and adjacent Delaware Mountains Permian section, including Brushy Canyon stratigraphy and relations along the western escarpment.

People: Philip B. King

King, P.B., 1948, Geology of the Southern Guadalupe Mountains, Texas: USGS Professional Paper 215, 183 p., https://doi.org/10.3133/pp215

text.headline: Hayes — USGS Professional Paper 446 New Mexico Guadalupes
text.text:
USGS Professional Paper 446 maps Guadalupe Mountains geology in New Mexico and discusses Delaware Mountain Group / Capitan shelf–reef–basin relations north of King's Texas map area.

People: Philip T. Hayes

Hayes, P.T., 1964, Geology of the Guadalupe Mountains, New Mexico: USGS Professional Paper 446, 69 p., https://doi.org/10.3133/pp446

media.alt: Hayes — USGS Professional Paper 446 New Mexico Guadalupes

text.headline: Harms — Brushy Canyon deep-water density-current deposit
text.text:
J. C. Harms interprets the Brushy Canyon Formation as a deep-water density-current deposit (GSA Bulletin). Widely cited turning point in Brushy Canyon process models.

People: John C. Harms

Harms, J.C., 1974, Brushy Canyon Formation, Texas: A deep-water density current deposit: Geological Society of America Bulletin, v. 85, p. 1763–1784.

media.alt: Harms — Brushy Canyon deep-water density-current deposit

text.headline: Rossen M.S. thesis — Brushy Canyon onlap area
text.text:
Christine Rossen M.S. thesis on Brushy Canyon sedimentology in the Guadalupe Mountains onlap area (University of Wisconsin–Madison). Cited as foundational outcrop work preceding later Exxon publications.

People: Christine Rossen

Rossen, C., 1985, Sedimentology of the Brushy Canyon Formation (Permian, Early Guadalupian) in the onlap area, Guadalupe Mountains, west Texas: M.S. thesis, University of Wisconsin–Madison, 314 p.

text.headline: Rossen and Sarg — 1987 AAPG abstract
text.text:
AAPG abstract on Brushy Canyon–Cherry Canyon Tongue sedimentology and regional correlation. Abstract favors turbidity currents over hypersaline density currents based on onlap geometry, channels, and shelfward correlation.

People: Christine Rossen, J. F. Sarg

Rossen, C., and Sarg, J.F., 1987, Sedimentology and regional correlation of a basinally restricted deep-water siliciclastic wedge: Brushy Canyon Formation–Cherry Canyon Tongue (Lower Guadalupian), Delaware Basin: AAPG Bulletin, v. 71 (abstract).

text.headline: Harms and Williamson — DMG saline density currents
text.text:
Harms and Williamson argue Delaware Mountain Group siltstones and channelized sandstones (including Brushy and Bell Canyon) were deposited by saline density currents in a density-stratified basin, contrasting with turbidity-current submarine-fan models.

People: John C. Harms, Charles R. Williamson

Harms, J.C., and Williamson, C.R., 1988, Deep-water density current deposits of Delaware Mountain Group (Permian), Delaware Basin, Texas and New Mexico: AAPG Bulletin, v. 72, p. 299–317.

media.alt: Harms and Williamson — DMG saline density currents

text.headline: Gardner 1992 — eolian-derived DMG turbidites
text.text:
WTGS symposium paper linking Delaware Mountain Group deep-water sandstones to eolian-derived turbidites along an arid carbonate platform, and discussing impacts on hydrocarbon recovery in DMG reservoirs (including Brushy Canyon-scale cyclicity).

People: Michael H. Gardner

Gardner, M.H., 1992, Sequence stratigraphy of eolian-derived turbidites: deep water sedimentation patterns along an arid carbonate platform and their impact on hydrocarbon recovery in Delaware Mountain Group reservoirs, west Texas, in Mruk, D.H., and Curran, B.C., eds., Permian Basin Exploration and Production Strategies: Applications of Sequence Stratigraphic and Reservoir Characterization Concepts: West Texas Geological Society, Inc. Symposium, Publication 92-91, p. 7–11.

text.headline: DOE Class III — Nash Draw Brushy Canyon Pool
text.text:
U.S. DOE Class III field demonstration (DE-FC22-95BC14941) at Nash Draw Pool, Eddy County, NM — integrated geology, engineering, and 3-D seismic to improve recovery from low-permeability Brushy Canyon slope–basin sandstones; later SPE papers emphasize compartmentalization and sweet-spot targeting.

People: F. David Martin, Mark B. Murphy, Bruce A. Stubbs, Bruce J. Uszynski, Bob A. Hardage, William W. Weiss

Martin, F.D., Murphy, M.B., Stubbs, B.A., Uszynski, B.J., Hardage, B.A., Kendall, R.P., Whitney, E.M., and Weiss, W.W., 1997, Reservoir characterization as a risk reduction tool at the Nash Draw Pool: SPE paper 38916 / later SPE Reservoir Evaluation & Engineering (SPE 56007-PA). DOE Cooperative Agreement DE-FC22-95BC14941.

text.headline: Zelt and Rossen — Brushy Canyon in deep-water atlas
text.text:
Chapter documenting geometry and continuity of Brushy Canyon deep-water sandstones and siltstones along Guadalupe–Delaware Mountains outcrops.

People: F. B. Zelt, Christine Rossen

Zelt, F.B., and Rossen, C., 1995, Geometry and continuity of deep-water sandstones and siltstones, Brushy Canyon Formation (Permian) Delaware Mountains, Texas, in Pickering, K.T., and others, eds., Atlas of Deep Water Environments: Springer.

text.headline: Gardner and Sonnenfeld — Brushy facies architecture
text.text:
PBS-SEPM / SEPM Permian Basin Section guidebook paper on stratigraphic changes in facies architecture of Brushy Canyon in Guadalupe Mountains National Park.

People: Michael H. Gardner, Mark D. Sonnenfeld

Gardner, M.H., and Sonnenfeld, M.D., 1996, Stratigraphic changes in architecture of the Permian Brushy Canyon Formation in Guadalupe Mountains National Park, west Texas, in DeMis, W.D., and Cole, A.G., eds., The Brushy Canyon Play in Outcrop and Subsurface: Concepts and Examples: SEPM, Permian Basin Section, Guidebook, Publication 96-38, p. 17–40.

text.headline: Hardage et al. 1998 — Brushy Canyon 3-D seismic imaging
text.text:
Geophysics paper from the Nash Draw DOE effort on 3-D seismic imaging and interpretation of thin-bed Brushy Canyon slope and basin reservoirs in the northwest Delaware Basin.

People: Bob A. Hardage, James L. Simmons Jr., Virginia M. Pendleton, Bruce A. Stubbs, Bruce J. Uszynski

Hardage, B.A., Simmons, J.L., Jr., Pendleton, V.M., Stubbs, B.A., and Uszynski, B.J., 1998, 3-D seismic imaging and interpretation of Brushy Canyon slope and basin thin-bed reservoirs, northwest Delaware Basin: Geophysics, v. 63, no. 5, p. 1507–1519, https://doi.org/10.1190/1.1444447

text.headline: Johnson M.S. (Mines) — Brushy outcrop and Cabin Lake reservoir
text.text:
Colorado School of Mines M.S. thesis integrating Brushy Canyon outcrop characterization in Guadalupe Mountains National Park with Cabin Lake Field (Eddy County, NM). Advisor: Michael H. Gardner.

People: Kyle R. Johnson

Johnson, K.R., 1998, Outcrop and reservoir characterization of the Brushy Canyon formation: Guadalupe Mountains National Park, West Texas, and Cabin Lake field, Eddy County, New Mexico: M.S. thesis, Colorado School of Mines, https://hdl.handle.net/11124/15090

text.headline: Beaubouef et al. — AAPG Course Note Series 40
text.text:
AAPG Continuing Education Course Note Series 40 field guide for the April 1999 Hedberg Field Research Conference on Brushy Canyon deep-water sandstones.

People: R. T. Beaubouef, Christine Rossen, F. B. Zelt, Morgan D. Sullivan, David C. Mohrig, David C. Jennette

Beaubouef, R.T., Rossen, C., Zelt, F.B., Sullivan, M.D., Mohrig, D.C., and Jennette, D.C., 1999, Deep-water sandstones, Brushy Canyon Formation, West Texas: Field guide for AAPG Hedberg Field Research Conference: AAPG Continuing Education Course Note Series 40, ~48 p., https://doi.org/10.1306/ce40695

media.alt: Beaubouef et al. — AAPG Course Note Series 40

text.headline: Kullman M.S. (Mines) — Brushy Canyon fractures
text.text:
Colorado School of Mines M.S. thesis on fracture networks and fault-zone features in Brushy Canyon deep-water sandstone. Advisors: Eric P. Nelson; Neil F. Hurley.

People: Aaron John Kullman

Kullman, A.J., 1999, Fracture networks and fault zone features in a deep water sandstone, Brushy Canyon formation, West Texas: M.S. thesis, Colorado School of Mines, https://hdl.handle.net/11124/15198

text.headline: Carr and Gardner 2000 — lower Brushy basin-floor fan
text.text:
Chapter in Fine-Grained Turbidite Systems describing architecture of a sandy lower Brushy Canyon basin-floor fan (sheets, distributary channels, cycle stacking).

People: Mary M. Carr, Michael H. Gardner

Carr, M.M., and Gardner, M.H., 2000, Portrait of a basin-floor fan for sandy deepwater systems, Permian Lower Brushy Canyon Formation, West Texas, in Bouma, A.H., and Stone, C.G., eds., Fine-grained turbidite systems: AAPG Memoir 72 / SEPM Special Publication 68, p. 215–231, https://doi.org/10.1306/m72703c20

text.headline: Gardner and Borer 2000 — slope-to-basin channel architecture
text.text:
Chapter in Fine-Grained Turbidite Systems comparing Brushy Canyon channel architecture along a slope-to-basin profile (cut–fill–spill hierarchy).

People: Michael H. Gardner, James M. Borer

Gardner, M.H., and Borer, J.M., 2000, Submarine channel architecture along a slope to basin profile, Brushy Canyon Formation, West Texas, in Bouma, A.H., and Stone, C.G., eds., Fine-grained turbidite systems: AAPG Memoir 72 / SEPM Special Publication 68, p. 195–214, https://doi.org/10.1306/m72703c19

text.headline: Wagerle M.S. (Mines) — middle Brushy Canyon architecture
text.text:
Colorado School of Mines M.S. thesis on proximal–distal vs along-strike variations in middle Brushy Canyon deep-water architecture, Delaware Mountains. Advisor: Michael H. Gardner.

People: Roger N. Wagerle

Wagerle, R.N., 2001, Deciphering proximal-distal from along-strike variations in the deep water architecture of the middle Brushy Canyon formation, Delaware Mountains, West Texas: M.S. thesis, Colorado School of Mines, https://hdl.handle.net/11124/15294

text.headline: Melick M.S. (Mines) — upper Brushy Canyon facies architecture
text.text:
Colorado School of Mines M.S. thesis on facies and sediment-body architecture of upper Brushy Canyon deep-water clastics, central Delaware Mountains. Advisor: Michael H. Gardner.

People: Jesse John Melick

Melick, J.J., 2002, Facies and sediment body architecture of Permian deep-water clastics, upper Brushy Canyon, central Delaware Mountains, West Texas, U.S.A.: M.S. thesis, Colorado School of Mines, https://hdl.handle.net/11124/15316

text.headline: Gardner et al. 2003 — process-response model for channels
text.text:
Marine and Petroleum Geology paper proposing a stratigraphic process-response model for submarine channels and related features from Brushy Canyon outcrops.

People: Michael H. Gardner, James M. Borer, Jesse J. Melick, Nicola Mavilla, Marieke Dechesne, Roger N. Wagerle

Gardner, M.H., Borer, J.M., Melick, J.J., Mavilla, N., Dechesne, M., and Wagerle, R.N., 2003, Stratigraphic process-response model for submarine channels and related features from studies of Permian Brushy Canyon outcrops, West Texas: Marine and Petroleum Geology, v. 20, p. 757–787, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marpetgeo.2003.07.004

text.headline: Romans M.S. (Mines) — Cutoff–Brushy–Cherry basinal cycle
text.text:
Colorado School of Mines M.S. thesis on sedimentation patterns of a Permian basinal cycle spanning upper Cutoff, Brushy Canyon, and lower Cherry Canyon across the western Delaware Basin. Advisor: Michael H. Gardner.

People: Brian W. Romans

Romans, B.W., 2003, Sedimentation patterns of a Permian basinal cycle, upper Cutoff, Brushy Canyon, and lower Cherry Canyon formations, western Delaware basin, west Texas and southeastern New Mexico, U.S.A.: M.S. thesis, Colorado School of Mines, https://hdl.handle.net/11124/15694

text.headline: Baptista M.S. (Mines) — Brushy Canyon basin-wide framework
text.text:
Colorado School of Mines M.S. thesis on deep-water depositional patterns and sequence stratigraphy of Brushy Canyon across the Delaware Basin. Advisor: Michael H. Gardner.

People: Noelia del Valle Baptista Brito

Baptista Brito, N. del V., 2004, Deep-water depositional patterns and sequence stratigraphic framework of the Permian Brushy Canyon formation across the Delaware Basin, West Texas and Southeastern New Mexico, U.S.A.: M.S. thesis, Colorado School of Mines, https://hdl.handle.net/11124/16747

text.headline: Bohacs et al. 2005 — production, destruction, dilution
text.text:
SEPM Special Publication 82 chapter framing organic-matter enrichment as production − (destruction + dilution). A widely cited source-rock pathway model applied in mudstone and petroleum-system discussions, including Delaware Basin / Brushy Canyon source–reservoir contexts.

People: Kevin M. Bohacs, George J. Grabowski Jr., Alan R. Carroll, Paul J. Mankiewicz, Kimberlee J. Miskell-Gerhardt, Jon R. Schwalbach, Mary Beth Wegner, J. A. Simó

Bohacs, K.M., Grabowski, G.J., Jr., Carroll, A.R., Mankiewicz, P.J., Miskell-Gerhardt, K.J., Schwalbach, J.R., Wegner, M.B., and Simó, J.A., 2005, Production, Destruction, and Dilution—The Many Paths to Source-Rock Development, in Harris, N.B., ed., The Deposition of Organic-Carbon-Rich Sediments: Models, Mechanisms, and Consequences: SEPM Special Publication 82, p. 61–101, https://doi.org/10.2110/pec.05.82.0061

text.headline: Borer Ph.D. (Mines) — middle Brushy Canyon channel modeling
text.text:
Colorado School of Mines Ph.D. dissertation on outcrop analysis and geologic modeling of submarine channels and related strata, middle Brushy Canyon. Advisors: Michael H. Gardner; Timothy A. Cross.

People: James M. Borer

Borer, J.M., 2005, Outcrop analysis and geologic modeling of submarine channels and related strata, Permian middle Brushy Canyon formation, West Texas, USA: Ph.D. dissertation, Colorado School of Mines, https://hdl.handle.net/11124/177744

text.headline: Kling Ph.D. (Mines) — Brushy Canyon starved margin
text.text:
Colorado School of Mines Ph.D. dissertation on deep-marine sedimentation patterns along a starved basin margin, Brushy Canyon, southern Delaware Mountains. Advisor: Michael H. Gardner.

People: Erik R. Kling

Kling, E.R., 2006, Patterns of deep marine sedimentation along a starved basin margin, Permian Brushy Canyon Formation, southern Delaware Mountains, West Texas, USA: Ph.D. dissertation, Colorado School of Mines, https://hdl.handle.net/11124/177784

text.headline: AAPG Atlas of Deep-Water Outcrops (SG 56)
text.text:
AAPG Studies in Geology 56 outcrop atlas compiling global deep-water case studies. Includes multiple Brushy Canyon chapters (among them Beacon Channel and related Guadalupe–Delaware Mountains examples) rather than a single paper entry.

People: Tor H. Nilsen, Roger D. Shew, Gary S. Steffens, Joseph R. J. Studlick

Nilsen, T.H., Shew, R.D., Steffens, G.S., and Studlick, J.R.J., eds., 2007, Atlas of Deep-Water Outcrops: AAPG Studies in Geology 56, https://doi.org/10.1306/St561240

text.headline: Hanggoro M.S. (Mines) — lower Brushy Canyon slope channels
text.text:
Colorado School of Mines M.S. thesis on facies and architecture of sandy slope channels, lower Brushy Canyon, Bitterwell Mountains. Advisor: Michael H. Gardner.

People: Diah Hanggoro

Hanggoro, D., 2007, Facies and architecture of sandy slope channels, Permian lower Brushy Canyon formation, Bitterwell Mountains, West Texas USA: M.S. thesis, Colorado School of Mines, https://hdl.handle.net/11124/15998

text.headline: Pyles et al. 2010 — Beacon Channel Complex 3D outcrop
text.text:
JSR paper documenting high-resolution 3D stratigraphy of the Beacon Channel Complex (upper Brushy Canyon), including hierarchical channel stories, sweep/swing migration, and concepts for sinuous slope-channel reservoirs; builds on the 2007 atlas chapter.

People: David R. Pyles, David C. Jennette, Mark Tomasso, Rick T. Beaubouef, Christine Rossen

Pyles, D.R., Jennette, D.C., Tomasso, M., Beaubouef, R.T., and Rossen, C., 2010, Concepts learned from a 3D outcrop of a sinuous slope channel complex: Beacon Channel Complex, Brushy Canyon Formation, West Texas, U.S.A.: Journal of Sedimentary Research, v. 80, p. 67–96, https://doi.org/10.2110/jsr.2010.009

text.headline: No 2021 — Brushy Canyon oil pay-zone characteristics
text.text:
Technical report on geophysical characteristics of Brushy Canyon oil pay zones in the Delaware Basin (channel–levee–lobe complexes sealed by organic-rich siltstone), with log examples from Roadrunner #2.

People: Young-Hwa No

No, Y.-H., 2021, Study on the Characteristics of Oil Pay Zone in the Brushy Canyon Formation, Delaware Mountain Group of the Delaware Basin: Journal of the Korean Society of Mineral and Energy Resources Engineers, v. 58, no. 2, p. 179–190, https://doi.org/10.32390/ksmer.2021.58.2.179
